headline: Chrome again exempts Google from user site data settings
summary: Google's Chrome browser has reportedly once more bypassed user-defined site data settings for its own services, raising renewed privacy concerns. This action allows Google to collect data without explicit user consent.
details: Google's Chrome browser is reportedly once again bypassing user-defined site data settings specifically for Google's own services. This means that even when users configure their browser to block third-party cookies or site data, Google's domains are exempt from these restrictions.

This exemption allows Google to continue tracking user activity across its various platforms, regardless of the privacy preferences set by the user. Critics argue this undermines user control over their personal data and browser privacy.

The issue has surfaced previously, indicating a pattern where Google prioritizes its data collection practices over user privacy controls within its own browser. This recurring behavior raises questions about Chrome's commitment to user privacy settings.
